$schema: F008 competitive comparison matrix — reused by docs/gtm/comparison/index.md and the marketing site (F003)
methodology: Every cell for CloudZero, Vantage, Jira Agents, and Anthropic Console is grounded in a live fetch of that vendor's own public site/docs on the date in dateVerified, with a direct quote in note. 'DIY' has no vendor to fetch, so its cells are an engineering-effort analysis (citation points back to this file's methodology, not a URL) and are more generous than a vendor cell would be: DIY marks 'partial' wherever a capability is achievable by hand-building it, not just 'no'. MeridianOS's own cells are grounded in this repo's code/tests, cited by file path, and include the same honesty discipline as docs/gtm/battle-card.md — including flagging where MeridianOS itself falls short (see meridianos.notes).

valueLegend.yes: Verified capability, shipped and documented today
valueLegend.no: Verified absence, or the dimension does not apply to this product's category
valueLegend.partial: Achievable or partially present, with a material caveat in the note

dimensions.label: Cross-vendor aggregation
dimensions.description: Aggregates AI spend/usage across more than one model vendor (e.g. Anthropic + OpenAI + DeepSeek) in one place.

dimensions.label: Per-task cost attribution
dimensions.description: Attributes cost to a specific unit of work (task/run/session/PR) — not just customer, product, team, or infrastructure dimensions.

dimensions.label: Inline enforcement
dimensions.description: Can stop a call BEFORE it is billed/forwarded when a budget is exceeded, vs. only reporting spend after the fact.

dimensions.label: Agent orchestration
dimensions.description: Runs/schedules a fleet of autonomous agents through a work loop (planning, execution, verification) rather than just observing or delegating one agent to one ticket.

dimensions.label: Model routing (cost opt)
dimensions.description: Automatically routes a task to a cheaper or more capable model based on complexity, as an active cost-optimization mechanism (not just reporting which model was used).

dimensions.label: Multi-tool integration
dimensions.description: Works across more than one work-management surface (e.g. Jira AND Azure DevOps AND Slack), not locked to a single tool's backlog.

dimensions.label: Real-time vs delayed
dimensions.description: How fresh the cost/usage data is: does it reflect a call the moment it happens, or only after a reporting delay (or not at all, if the product has no cost dimension)?

dimensions.label: Open source core
dimensions.description: Is the product's core implementation publicly inspectable (open-source repo), or closed/proprietary?

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: "unifies cost and usage from every AI platform, cloud provider, and SaaS tool into dimensional cost intelligence" — 40+ integrations including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, AWS, Azure, GCP.

per-task-cost-attribution.note: "Follow a dollar of AI spend through customer, feature, workflow, and model" — allocates to customer/product/feature/team dimensions via configured tags, but there is no automatic task_id/run_id/session dimension captured per call the way an agent-run ledger would.

inline-enforcement.note: May 2026 launch of the "financial control plane for AI" describes attribution, multi-dimensional allocation, and real-time spend visibility — no capability to block or stop a call before it's billed. "Real-time spend starts with telemetry, not the monthly bill" is about visibility speed, not enforcement.

agent-orchestration.note: AI Hub embeds cost visibility into existing agentic workflows (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI) via an MCP server — it observes agents that already exist, it does not schedule, plan, or run them.

model-routing.note: No automated cost-based model routing described anywhere on the platform pages; the product reports which model was used, it does not choose which model to use.

multi-tool-integration.note: Connects cost data to "GitHub, Jira, Slack, PagerDuty, and Datadog" plus an open MCP server for any compatible agent/tool.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: CloudZero's own "streaming telemetry" claims near-real-time capture ("a runaway inference bill surfaces in seconds") when a customer instruments calls directly through it — but the Anthropic Admin API connector it also offers inherits Anthropic's own ~5-minute reporting lag (see the Anthropic Console row), so freshness depends on which ingestion path a customer actually uses.

open-source-core.note: Closed-source commercial SaaS platform; no public source repository referenced anywhere on the site.

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: Describes itself as "the system of record for allocating and optimizing cloud, SaaS, and AI costs" across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

per-task-cost-attribution.note: The finest attribution dimensions documented for the Anthropic integration are Billing Account (Organization), Account (Workspace), API key, model, and user — no task/job/run_id dimension is described anywhere in the connector docs.

inline-enforcement.note: Ships "Custom Cost Alerts" and "Budget Alerts" — alerting/monitoring terminology throughout; no documented mechanism blocks a request or stops spend before it's incurred.

agent-orchestration.note: "AI-Enabled FinOps" refers to querying Vantage's own data via ChatGPT or Claude as a chat interface, not orchestrating or scheduling AI agents.

model-routing.note: Offers cost recommendations and commitment-plan autopilot for cloud infrastructure, but no automated per-task model routing for AI calls.

multi-tool-integration.note: 20+ integrations spanning AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Datadog, Snowflake, and more.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: "Both Anthropic data sources refresh once daily" — explicitly slower than Anthropic's own native Usage API, which itself already lags ~5 minutes behind the call.

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: Jira Agents (Spring 2026 seasonal release) is a task-delegation feature, not a cost tool — the release page contains no discussion of spend, budgets, or cross-vendor cost visibility at all.

per-task-cost-attribution.note: No pricing, cost, or usage-governance concept is mentioned anywhere on the release page for the agents feature.

inline-enforcement.note: No budget or spend concept exists for Jira Agents, so there is nothing to enforce against.

agent-orchestration.note: "Delegate work items to Claude and get draft PRs back for review" and "Assign tasks or @mention agents directly from Jira" — this is manual, one-agent-per-work-item delegation across a roster of third-party agents (Copilot, Cursor, custom Studio agents), not an autonomous multi-agent scheduling loop.

model-routing.note: A human/team picks which agent handles a ticket; no automated cost-based routing between models is described.

multi-tool-integration.note: Connects OUT to many third-party agent tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Canva, Figma, Hubspot, Intercom), but the work-item source of truth is Jira only — no evidence of pulling backlog items IN from Azure DevOps, Linear, or other trackers.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: Not applicable in practice: there is no cost/spend data surfaced by this feature at all, real-time or otherwise.

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: The Usage & Cost Admin API is explicitly scoped to "your organization's API usage" on Anthropic's own platform — it has no concept of another vendor's spend, by design (no vendor aggregates a competitor).

per-task-cost-attribution.note: "Filtering & grouping: Filter by API key, workspace, model, service tier, context window, data residency, or speed (beta)" — every dimension is infrastructure-shaped; there is no job/task/tag/label dimension anywhere in the documented API.

inline-enforcement.note: Workspaces support "Spend limits: Cap monthly spending for a workspace" as distinct from "Spend notifications: Configure alerts when spending reaches certain thresholds" — the existence of a separate 'cap' control suggests more than alerting, but the docs never state whether a request is actually blocked once the cap is hit. Unresolved and explicitly NOT claimed as soft or hard either way; contrast with OpenAI's project budgets, which are documented as soft ("API requests will continue to be processed... it does not enforce a hard cap on spending").

agent-orchestration.note: Workspaces organize API keys, members, and spend limits — they do not schedule or run agents.

model-routing.note: No automated cost-based routing between models; the API reports which model was called, it does not choose one.

multi-tool-integration.note: Single-tool console/API for Anthropic's own platform; third-party FinOps partners (CloudZero, Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb, Vantage) provide the tool-spanning views, not Anthropic itself.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: "Usage and cost data typically appears within 5 minutes of API request completion, though delays may occasionally be longer" — reporting, not real-time.

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: Trivial in principle: a team that writes its own logging wrapper around each vendor SDK can log all of them to one place. Not a product claim — an engineering-effort assessment, since there's no vendor to verify against.

per-task-cost-attribution.note: Achievable only by building the equivalent of a task/run/session-tagged ledger from scratch — real engineering effort, not a checkbox. No off-the-shelf reference implementation exists; most teams that log spend stop at request-level logs, not work-item attribution.

inline-enforcement.note: Possible if a team builds request-time budget checks into a proxy of their own — but most DIY cost-logging setups only log after the response returns, which cannot block a call already in flight.

agent-orchestration.note: Cost-logging scripts and an autonomous multi-agent scheduler are unrelated engineering efforts; building cost visibility does not get a team a fleet-orchestration loop for free.

model-routing.note: A team can hand-code if/else routing by task complexity, but it is bespoke logic maintained per-team, not a reusable capability.

multi-tool-integration.note: By definition, a team can call whatever tool's API it wants — full flexibility is the point of building it yourself.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: Entirely dependent on what's built — could be real-time (inline proxy) or delayed (batch log analysis). No default answer.

open-source-core.note: A team's own code is, by definition, theirs to inspect and own — no vendor lock-in.

meridianos.name: MeridianOS
meridianos.notes: MeridianOS's cells are grounded in this repo's own code/tests, cited by file path (verifiable by reading the file, not a live external URL). One cell below is a real, current shortfall, not a marketing gap: open-source-core is 'no' as of 2026-07-21 — the repo at github.com/gravity-7/meridianos-core returns 404 to an unauthenticated request, i.e. it is currently private, not published open source, despite the architecture being designed to eventually be one. See 'Where MeridianOS falls short' in index.md.

cross-vendor-aggregation.note: Three registered, gateway-routable providers today (Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenRouter), one ledger. A fourth OpenAI-wire endpoint (local Ollama) is conformance-tested but not yet a registered provider (tests/ollama-e2e.test.mjs).

per-task-cost-attribution.note: Every ledger row carries tenant, agent, session, task, and run_id — the dimension every vendor and observability tool above lacks.

inline-enforcement.note: Verdict is computed before forwarding; a deny short-circuits to a non-retryable 403 and never dials the provider. Proven at the process level offline (a real claude CLI exits non-zero against a real gateway instance in the exit-confirm test). NOT yet proven with a captured deny row against live paid traffic — scripts/dogfood-deny-run.mjs exists to close this gap but has not been run (see index.md's dogfood data section).

agent-orchestration.note: A watchdog tick drives planning, launching agents in isolated worktrees, and verification across multiple swappable harnesses (claude-code, opencode, antigravity) — an actual scheduling loop, not single-agent delegation.

model-routing.note: Routes tasks to a model tier (simple/medium/complex) by declared complexity, an active cost-optimization mechanism none of the competitors above ship.

multi-tool-integration.citation: azure-devops-source.mjs (untracked, no test coverage as of 2026-07-21)
multi-tool-integration.note: The harness/scheduler side genuinely spans multiple agent tools. The ADO backlog connector exists as a 340-line prototype with zero test coverage and is not yet committed to the repo — it is a documented roadmap item, not a shipped capability. Do not claim ADO/Jira/Slack integration as delivered.

real-time-vs-delayed.note: Enforcement and metering happen inline, in the same request, before the response returns — there is no polling delay because there is no separate reporting pipeline to lag behind.

open-source-core.note: Verified private as of this date. The architecture is designed to be provider/harness-agnostic and tenant-agnostic in a way that would support open-sourcing the core, but it has not actually been published as open source yet. Listing this as a win would be false.
